title: Magnemite's Floating Has a Magnetic Catch

direction.premise: Magnemite’s side units keep it airborne while drawing iron objects from over 300 feet away.
direction.audiencePromise: See how Magnemite’s floating system doubles as a long-range iron pull.
direction.openLoop: How can Magnemite float and still pull distant iron?
direction.payoff: Magnemite’s side units solve two problems at once: staying airborne and drawing in iron.
direction.engagementQuestion: Clever two-job design, or too much magnetic power?

voice.instructions: Speak quickly, warmly, and clearly. Stress "iron" and "two jobs," then pause before the final either-or question.

scenes.headline: FLOATING, BUT IRON FLIES
scenes.narration: Magnemite floats, but iron can come flying.
scenes.caption: FLOATING HAS A CATCH

scenes.headline: ONE SYSTEM, TWO JOBS
scenes.narration: The same side units that keep it airborne generate powerful magnetism.
scenes.caption: AIRBORNE AND MAGNETIC

scenes.headline: THE PULL REACHES 300 FEET
scenes.narration: That pull reaches iron objects more than three hundred feet away.
scenes.caption: IRON OBJECTS • OVER 300 FEET

scenes.headline: DISTANT IRON GETS DRAWN IN
scenes.narration: Distance is the puzzle: faraway iron still gets drawn in.
scenes.caption: DISTANCE DOESN’T STOP THE PULL

scenes.headline: THE UNITS DO BOTH
scenes.narration: The units do two jobs at once: hold Magnemite up and pull iron.
scenes.caption: HOLD IT UP • PULL IRON

scenes.headline: CLEVER OR TOO POWERFUL?
scenes.narration: Clever two-job design, or too much magnetic power?
scenes.caption: CLEVER DESIGN OR TOO MUCH?
